podcast.title: Purchased "Louie Louie" Songwriting Rights (1959)
podcast.body: In 1959, the owner of Flip Records acquired the songwriting rights to "Louie Louie" and several other songs from Richard Berry for $750. "he sold his songwriting rights to Louis Louis and several of his other songs to the own Flip Records for $750."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Audition Label for Sun Records
podcast.body: Flip was a new record label established by Sam Phillips as a cost-cutting measure while he faced financial difficulties. Its purpose was to release records, like Carl Perkins's first single "Movie Mag," that did not pay union scale. Distributed only locally around Tennessee, these releases served as "audition records," allowing Phillips to gauge an artist's local performance without incurring full royalty payments, expensive shipping costs, or large print runs. "Rather, he put them out on a new label, Flip, that didn't pay union scale."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 36: "Blue Suede Shoes" by Carl Perkins

podcast.title: Pressured Berry for Follow-ups
podcast.body: After "Louie Louie" became a local hit, Flip Records pressured Richard Berry to produce follow-ups specifically to that song, rather than allowing him to explore new material. "Flip Records started pressuring him to make follow ups to Louis Louis, rather than to do anything new."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Richard Berry's Label for "Louie Louie"
podcast.body: Richard Berry's original 1957 recording of "Louie Louie" was released on Flip Records, a small label. "By this time Barry had left modern records, and Louis Louis was on a small label, Flip Records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
